meta.title: Post-launch connections: analytics, search, behaviour tracking and the deploy that carries them
meta.lead: How a freshly launched site gets its GA4, Search Console and Hotjar wired up and verified, almost all of it through Claude prompts. If you remember one thing: an env change is not live until the next build, and nothing is verified until you have seen it in the live HTML.
meta.frequency: Once per site, in launch week

tasks.label: Get the live site and your branch
tasks.hint: Tasks 1.1–1.3 · start of every post-launch session

tasks.label: Check the analytics code
tasks.hint: Tasks 2.1–2.2 · one prompt, once per site

tasks.label: Google Analytics 4
tasks.hint: Tasks 3.1–3.8 · find or create, tag, settings, verify

tasks.label: Google Search Console
tasks.hint: Tasks 4.1–4.6 · verify, sitemap, indexing, owner, GA link

tasks.hint: Task 6.1 · one prompt checks and fixes

source.note: Converted from SOP-POST-LAUNCH-CONNECTIONS.md, captured on the Ridge & Falls launch, 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-11

items.t: Purpose
items.d: Gets a newly launched site reporting to Google Analytics 4, verified in Google Search Console and recording in Hotjar, with each change published and checked on the live site.

items.t: In scope
items.d: Netlify-hosted Next.js sites built from the HGM template, once the domain is live. HGM-SOP-WEB-005 hands the site over here.

items.t: Out of scope
items.d: The launch itself (DNS cutover, go-live), the client-facing analytics walkthrough in docs/ANALYTICS-SETUP.md, and paid media tags beyond the Meta Pixel block already in the codebase.

blocks.t: Five standing rules
blocks.d: True on every post-launch session.

items.t: Start from the live main, on your own branch
items.d: Task 1.1 proves main is what's live and makes your branch. Nothing is changed on main directly.

items.t: An env change is not live until the next build
items.d: Redeploy after every change to GA_MEASUREMENT_ID, HOTJAR_SITE_ID or GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION, then check the live HTML.

items.t: Analytics variables go in Netlify's Production context only
items.d: Never in .env.local, so dev and preview traffic stays out of the client's reports.

items.t: One web team login for everything Google
items.d: Create Analytics and Search Console as hgmwebteam@gmail.com, so one login holds both and task 4.6 works first time.

items.t: Never print or paste an env value
items.d: Check lengths, not contents. A value pasted into a chat, an Asana comment or a prompt is a key that has to be rotated.

items.t: VS Code or the Claude desktop app, with Claude Code signed in
items.d: Every task runs from a Claude prompt. First time on this computer? HGM-SOP-WEB-002 Phase 1 installs the tools.

items.t: The Netlify connector
items.d: Connected in Claude, with access to the client's Netlify team. Claude uses it to check what's live, set environment variables and redeploy.

items.t: The site's .env.local entry in 1Password
items.d: Task 1.2 copies it in (HGM-SOP-WEB-001).

items.t: The web team login
items.d: hgmwebteam@gmail.com, for Google Analytics and Search Console, and invited to the client's Netlify, Supabase and Resend accounts (task 1.3).

items.t: The agency Hotjar login
items.d: hgmwebteam. It holds one organisation per client (Hotjar's container for that client; plan limits and seats are per organisation); sites are added inside the client's organisation, never at the top level.

blocks.text: Phase 1 — Get the live site and your branch
blocks.d: Start of every post-launch session. One prompt gets the latest code, proves it is what's live and makes your branch.

blocks.t: Open the site and make your branch
blocks.d: Open the site's folder in VS Code (an empty folder if this computer has never had the site), or start Claude Code in the Claude desktop app, then paste the prompt. Your branch is your own copy of the code to work on, named post-launch.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.note: fill in the three angle-bracket values
body.text:
I'm starting post-launch connections (HGM-SOP-WEB-003) for
<client>, live at https://<domain>. Get me set up:

1. If this folder isn't the site's repository, clone
   https://github.com/hgmwebteam/<site-name>.git and open it.
2. Switch to main and pull the latest. If there are changes
   here I don't recognise, stop and show me. Discard nothing.
3. Prove main is what's live: check <domain> points at this
   site's Netlify project, and that the latest production
   deploy was built from origin/main's commit. If the Netlify
   connector can't see the site, stop and tell me to do
   task 1.3 first.
4. Create a branch named post-launch from main and switch
   to it.

Tell me plainly if anything doesn't match. Make no other
changes.

blocks.t: Add the .env.local file, then have Claude check it
blocks.d: Copy the site's .env.local entry from 1Password into a file named .env.local in the project folder (HGM-SOP-WEB-001), then paste the prompt. A file copied from the template looks like a broken site: empty listings, missing photos. If keys are blank, the 1Password entry needs updating (WEB-001 Phase 2).

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Check .env.local: list every key with the LENGTH of its value.
Never print a value. Tell me which keys are blank. Do not
fetch or write any secret yourself.

blocks.t: Check the web team is on the client's Netlify, Supabase and Resend
blocks.d: Sign in to each as hgmwebteam@gmail.com and confirm the client's Netlify team, Supabase project and Resend account are listed. If one is missing, invite hgmwebteam@gmail.com to it the way HGM-SOP-WEB-004 tasks 2.1, 4.2 and 4.7 do. The team's automations connect through this account, with nothing else to set up.

blocks.text: Phase 2 — Check the analytics code is in place
blocks.d: Once per site. One prompt reads the code; you act only if it changed something.

blocks.t: Ask Claude to check the analytics code
blocks.d: The site's page head carries three blocks, each switched on by a Netlify variable and silent while it is unset. The prompt confirms they are there, adds any that is missing, and confirms there is no GA4 purchase event: bookings are reported to Meta from the server, so a browser purchase event would count every booking twice.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Check this site's analytics code and tell me what you find
before you change anything. Change code only on this branch.

1. app/layout.tsx must have three blocks, modelled on the
   Meta Pixel block. Each reads a server-side variable (no
   NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix), checks the value's shape, and
   renders nothing while the variable is unset:
   - GA_MEASUREMENT_ID (G-...): gtag.js plus gtag('config'),
     strategy lazyOnload
   - HOTJAR_SITE_ID (digits): the Hotjar snippet (hjsv 6),
     strategy lazyOnload
   - GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION (a token): the
     google-site-verification meta tag, through Next's
     metadata.verification.google
2. All three names must be in .env.example and in the docs'
   environment list.
3. There must be NO GA4 purchase event. Bookings reach Meta
   from the server, so one would double count.

If anything is missing, add it on the Meta Pixel pattern,
commit it on this branch and tell me what you changed. If
everything is there, say so and change nothing.

blocks.t: If Claude changed code, take it live before Phase 3
blocks.d: If Claude changed nothing in 2.1, go to Phase 3. Otherwise the variables in Phases 3 to 5 do nothing until this code is live, so paste the prompt. It opens a pull request (a request to merge your branch into main), which you merge on GitHub the way HGM-SOP-WEB-002 Phase 6 does, then checks the live site was rebuilt from it. Task 6.1 comes back here if it changes code too.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Take my branch live:

1. Push this branch and give me the link to open a pull
   request into main. Do not merge it yourself.
2. When I tell you it's merged, switch to main, pull, and use
   the Netlify connector to confirm the latest production
   deploy was built from the merge commit.
3. If production did not rebuild, deploy main with the
   Netlify connector from a clean copy of main's committed
   files only. Never upload this folder: it holds .env.local
   and build files, and Netlify returns errors.
4. Fetch https://<domain>/ and confirm the change is live.

Then put me on a new post-launch branch made from main.

blocks.d: Signed in as hgmwebteam@gmail.com throughout. Use the client's own account if they have one; create one for them if they don't.

blocks.t: Find the client's Google Analytics, or create an account for them
blocks.d: Ask the account manager whether the client already has Google Analytics, and paste the prompt to look for it in the code. If they have an account, send the message below, then use their property for this domain (or create one inside their account) and go to 3.3. If not, open Admin → Create → Account, name it after the client, then add a property named after the site with a web data stream for the apex domain (the address with no www).

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Check whether <client> already uses Google Analytics. Search
Resources/Page HTML (the old site's pages from WEB-004, if
this folder has them) and the live https://<domain>/ for a
GA4 ID (G-...), an old Universal Analytics ID (UA-...) or a
Tag Manager container (GTM-...). Tell me each ID you find and
where. Make no changes.

body.label: Message for the account manager
body.text:
<client> already has Google Analytics. Please ask them to add
hgmwebteam@gmail.com as an Administrator under Admin → Account
access management, so we can connect their new site.

body.t: Creating a property in the client's account
body.text: Read the account name at the top of Admin first. A property lands in whichever account is showing, and the web team login sees every client's. Move a misplaced property; recreating it changes its measurement ID.

blocks.t: Add the client as Administrator
blocks.d: Only if you created the account in 3.1. Admin → Account access management → Add users, enter the client's Google login from the account manager, role Administrator.

blocks.t: Set GA_MEASUREMENT_ID and redeploy
blocks.d: Copy the measurement ID (the G-… code) from Admin → Data streams → your stream, then paste the prompt with it.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.note: fill in the G- ID and the domain
body.text:
Using the Netlify connector, set GA_MEASUREMENT_ID to <G-ID>
in this site's Production context only (never .env.local),
then redeploy production from main. Never deploy by uploading
this folder: it holds .env.local and build files, and Netlify
returns errors.

When the deploy is live, fetch https://<domain>/ and confirm
<G-ID> is in both the gtag/js script URL and the
gtag('config') call. Retry every 30 seconds for up to
3 minutes before you call it a failure.

blocks.t: Turn on page views for browser history events
blocks.d: Admin → Data streams → your stream → Enhanced measurement → gear icon → Page views → Show advanced settings → Page changes based on browser history events: ON. The site fires one page view per full load and relies on this setting for client-side navigations.

body.caption: Enhanced measurement → Page views → Show advanced settings: tick Page changes based on browser history events, then Save.

blocks.t: Set data retention to 14 months
blocks.d: Admin → Data collection and modification → Data retention → Event data retention: 14 months. The default is 2.

body.caption: Admin → Data retention: Event data set to 14 months, then Save.

blocks.t: Set the property time zone and currency
blocks.d: Admin → Property details. Time zone = the site's, from BRAND.timezone in the codebase. Currency USD.

body.caption: Admin → Property details: choose the site's time zone (still unset here) and US Dollar.

blocks.t: Define internal traffic and set the filter to Active
blocks.d: Admin → Data streams → your stream → Configure tag settings → Define internal traffic: add the office and home IPs. Then Admin → Data filters → Internal Traffic and set its state to Active. It ships in Testing, which does nothing to reports.

blocks.t: Verify in Realtime with a real visit
blocks.d: Open the live site in a browser, then Reports → Realtime. You should appear as an active user within a minute.

body.t: Two things that look like failure and are not
body.text: The "Data collection isn't active" banner can take 48 hours to clear: ignore it if Realtime works. Google's Test your website button may not see the tag, because it loads after window.load.

blocks.d: Signed in as hgmwebteam@gmail.com, the same login as Phase 3. A URL-prefix property (one exact address) verified with an HTML tag.

blocks.t: Add a URL-prefix property and copy the HTML tag token
blocks.d: Add property → URL prefix, enter https://<domain> (the apex; www and http redirect to it). If the Domain dialog opens, click try a URL prefix property instead. Under the verification methods choose HTML tag and copy the content value only, not the whole tag.

body.caption: The property list: a URL-prefix property shows as its full address (https://…); a Domain property says so underneath.

blocks.t: Set GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION, redeploy, then click Verify
blocks.d: Paste the prompt with the token. When Claude confirms the tag is live, go back to Search Console and click Verify.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.note: fill in the token and the domain
body.text:
Using the Netlify connector, set GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION to
<TOKEN> in this site's Production context only (never
.env.local), then redeploy production from main. Never
deploy by uploading this folder: it holds .env.local and
build files, and Netlify returns errors.

When the deploy is live, fetch https://<domain>/ and confirm
the google-site-verification meta tag's content equals
<TOKEN>. Retry every 30 seconds for up to 3 minutes before
you call it a failure.

blocks.t: Submit the sitemap
blocks.d: Sitemaps → Add a new sitemap: sitemap.xml, then Submit. Pages set to noindex are left out of it on purpose.

body.caption: Sitemaps → Add a new sitemap: type sitemap.xml and Submit. The submitted sitemap should read Success.

blocks.t: Request indexing for the main pages
blocks.d: Request indexing for at least the pages below, and every other page too if you want. Paste the prompt for their full addresses, then for each one: URL Inspection → paste it → Request indexing. The daily quota is small: if Search Console says you have reached it, request the rest the next day.

items: The home page: https://<domain>/
The stays page: https://<domain>/stays
Every listing page, for example https://<domain>/listing1, https://<domain>/listing2 and so on

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Read https://<domain>/sitemap.xml and list, one per line, the
full address of the home page, the stays page and every
listing page, then every other page. Make no changes.

body.caption: URL inspection's result card: Request indexing is on the right.

blocks.t: Add the client as Owner
blocks.d: Settings → Users and permissions → Add user, enter the client's Google login, permission Owner.

body.caption: Settings → Users and permissions: Add user, then choose Owner. Emails hidden here.

blocks.t: Link Google Analytics to Search Console
blocks.d: In Google Analytics: Admin → Product links → Search Console links → Link, choose the property you verified in 4.2, then Next. The link needs a login that owns the Search Console property and is Editor or above in Analytics; hgmwebteam@gmail.com is both.

body.caption: GA Admin → Product links → Search Console links → Link: choose the verified property, then Next.

blocks.d: Check first, then the client's organisation, install, privacy settings before the first recording, and a real browser visit to verify.

blocks.t: Check whether the client already runs Hotjar
blocks.d: So you never create a second Hotjar site for one that already has one. Get the client's other websites from the account manager, then paste the prompt.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Check whether <client> already uses Hotjar. Fetch the home
page of each of these sites and look for an hjid:
<domain-1>, <domain-2>, <domain-3>.
Also search Resources/Page HTML (the old site's pages, if
this folder has them) and any Google Tag Manager container
you can see. Report each hjid you find and where. Make no
changes.

blocks.t: Open the client's organisation in Hotjar
blocks.d: Log in as hgmwebteam. Switch to the client's organisation. If none exists, choose Add as a New Client Organization and name it after the client, not the site: plan limits and team seats are per organisation.

blocks.t: Add the site, then set HOTJAR_SITE_ID and redeploy
blocks.d: Inside the client's organisation, add the site for the apex domain and copy its numeric Site ID, then paste the prompt with it.

body.caption: Hotjar → Sites & Organizations → New site: choose the client's organisation first, never the top level.
Once the site is added, its Site ID is at the top right of the install page. That number is HOTJAR_SITE_ID.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.note: fill in the Site ID and the domain
body.text:
Using the Netlify connector, set HOTJAR_SITE_ID to <SITE-ID>
in this site's Production context only (never .env.local),
then redeploy production from main. Never deploy by uploading
this folder: it holds .env.local and build files, and Netlify
returns errors.

When the deploy is live, fetch https://<domain>/ and confirm
the Hotjar snippet carries <SITE-ID>. Then fetch
https://static.hotjar.com/c/hotjar-<SITE-ID>.js?sv=6 and
confirm it returns 200 and names site_id <SITE-ID>.

blocks.t: Visit the site in a real browser
blocks.d: Open the live site in a browser with no ad blocker (Brave and uBlock hide Hotjar) and click through two pages. Hotjar marks a site installed only after its script runs in a real browser; Claude's fetch does not count.

blocks.t: Fix the privacy settings before the first recording
blocks.d: In the site's settings: turn keystroke capture off (it was on by default on Ridge & Falls). Add URL exclusions for paths containing /admin, /manual, /checkout and /confirmation. Add the office IPs to IP blocking.

body.t: The confirmation page prints guest name and email as text
body.text: Without the exclusion, a session recording captures personal data. Set the exclusions before any real traffic is recorded.

blocks.t: Invite the client
blocks.d: Team → Invite, and enter the client's login.
Once, after Phases 3 to 5. One prompt checks the stays page and a listing page, and fixes the code if it needs it.

blocks.t: Ask Claude to check the structured data
blocks.d: Structured data is the hidden description of each page that search and answer engines read. Paste the prompt, then test the two addresses it gives you in Google's Rich Results Test (search.google.com/test/rich-results). If Claude changed code, take it live the way task 2.2 does, then test again.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text:
Check the structured data (JSON-LD) on https://<domain>/stays
and one listing page.

1. Fetch both pages and pull out every JSON-LD block.
2. Look for one @id emitted twice with different content,
   such as a thin copy of each rental in the stays page's
   ItemList. Google merges the two and reports critical
   issues on every listing.
3. Check each entity against Google's documentation for its
   type, fetched now, not remembered: every required
   property, and the recommended ones where the data is real.

If you find a problem, fix it on this branch with one builder
function per entity (for example vacationRentalJsonLd in
lib/seo.ts), used by every page that mentions it. Leave out
anything you would have to invent, such as review dates or
bed types. Commit it and tell me what changed.

Finish by giving me both addresses to test in Google's Rich
Results Test. The aim is zero critical issues on each.

blocks.text: A client change request arrives during launch week
The pattern, in order. Every example shipped on Ridge & Falls followed it.

items.t: Locate the code from the screenshot or chat request
items.d: If the screenshot shows something "missing" on a dev box, check the data feed before the code: see task 1.2.

items.t: Edit, then run the checks
items.d: Ask Claude to run tsc, vitest and verify:brand.

items.t: Render through the real stylesheet for a one-look check
items.d: Use the Playwright harness so you are looking at the actual output, not a guess.

items.t: Record the decision
items.d: In CLAUDE.md and the team manual's Updates.

items.t: Commit, take it live, check it
items.d: Task 2.2 takes the branch live and confirms the change is on the live site.

items.t: A changed asset is a new filename
items.d: Static assets are cached immutable for a year. Ship wordmark-light-compact.svg, collection-*.webp, local-favorites-mclemore-resort-v3.webp — never overwrite in place.

items.t: Keep the client's swatches even when contrast fails
items.d: Document the contrast ratio at the declaration and tell the client the passing alternative. Do not silently change their colour.

items.t: Blur is often the sizes hint, not the file
items.d: The Local Favorites portrait crop was blurry because of the srcset sizes hint, not the images. Check the hint before regenerating assets.

blocks.t: If you are stuck
blocks.text: Ask Claude first, with the task number and what you see. Then Kyle Zinger (Web & Content Specialist) in the Web Team Google Chat group. Anything that needs the client — access to their Google Analytics, a missing invite — goes through the client's account manager, never the client directly.

items: Main confirmed as what's live; post-launch branch made from it; .env.local filled (lengths checked, not values)
hgmwebteam@gmail.com is a member of the client's Netlify, Supabase and Resend accounts
Analytics blocks present in app/layout.tsx, names documented, no purchase event; any code change merged and live
GA4: the client's own account used, or a new one created for them with the client as Administrator
GA_MEASUREMENT_ID set in Production → redeployed → tag in the live HTML → Realtime shows a visit
History events on; retention 14 months; time zone and currency set; internal traffic filter Active
Search Console URL-prefix property verified with the HTML tag; sitemap submitted
Home page, stays page and every listing page requested for indexing
Client added as Search Console Owner; Google Analytics linked to Search Console
Hotjar site inside the client's organisation; HOTJAR_SITE_ID set → redeployed → installed after a real browser visit
Hotjar keystrokes off, private pages excluded, office IPs blocked, client invited
Structured data on the stays page and a listing page: zero critical issues in the Rich Results Test
blocks.prompt: Check this site's post-launch setup against the final checklist below. For each line, say pass or fail and give the evidence: what you fetched, a URL, or what a dashboard shows. Make no changes.

items: docs/ANALYTICS-SETUP.md in the site repo — the client-facing walkthrough for GA4, Search Console and Hotjar
HGM-SOP-WEB-001 — env files in 1Password
HGM-SOP-WEB-002 — take a website change request from Asana to live (branch, preview, merge)
HGM-SOP-WEB-004 — the build, where the web team is invited to the client's Netlify, Supabase and Resend
HGM-SOP-WEB-005 — pre-launch and the cutover, which hands the site to this SOP

rows: Working draft converted from the Ridge & Falls launch-week notes, for Brandon. Not yet approved.

Loom review layout (house style v1.9). Roles, definitions and troubleshooting removed: terms are explained where first used, and each fix sits in the task it belongs to. Standing rules shortened; prerequisites collapse; an If you are stuck note; a copy-to-Claude button on the final checklist; links to other SOPs open in the portal.
Ten screenshots from the Awayframes launch added to tasks 4.4–6.3 (Google Analytics, Search Console, Hotjar), cropped and ringed.

Simplified around Claude prompts. Phase 1 gets main, proves it is live, makes a branch and checks .env.local, and checks the web team is on the client's Netlify, Supabase and Resend. The shallow-clone deploy phase is gone: code goes live through a merge, variables through one connector prompt. GA4 starts by finding the client's account or creating one for them, with no property move. Terminal commands, most expected results, Google Signals, the booking event, the DNS property choice and the ownership map removed. Indexing lists the pages to request. The analytics code check and the structured data check are one prompt each.

blocks.quote: "Prove you are looking at the live site before you change it. Then remember that nothing you set is live until the next build, and nothing is verified until you have seen it in the live HTML."
blocks.aside_d: Kyle — Web Team Google Chat group
